ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian sanctions instruments under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and the FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) framework for domestic and foreign PEPs, their relatives, and close associates. Where United States dollar clearing or escrow payment rails are utilized, OFAC SDN screening is required by correspondent banks. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and complex or opaque ownership structures, including independent source-of-funds documentation, negative-media inquiry, and continuous transaction monitoring. A written compliance program and audit trail are required under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance, with suspicious transaction reporting to FINTRAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises en ligne (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, and the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, s 88, the legal person's name must be in French in the material sense. A name may contain a French word, a French expression, or an acceptable transliterated or francized form of a foreign expression; proper nouns and registered trade-marks are exceptional. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters for the REQ name-search and registration process.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: loan, prêt, lending, financement without required licences
royal, imperial, crown, government, ministry, ministère
commission, committee, council, conseil where it falsely implies a public authority
Québec, Canada where the name misrepresents a public instrumentality or national origin
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file, within 30 days after notice of refusal, a written request for review with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec under An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, s 34(1). The review submission must include the refusal notice, a fresh name-search report, proposed amendments to the name, or written representations establishing distinguishability and compatibility with the Charter of the French Language. If the review is unsuccessful, judicial recourse may be commenced in the Superior Court of Quebec within the applicable prescriptive period, or the applicant may file a new incorporation request with a modified distinguishing element and pay the applicable filing fees.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally not acceptable as the sole registered office for a statutory factoring and trade-finance entity. The Registraire des entreprises du Québec requires an actual, serviced physical address in Quebec for service of process and official communications. For an ISIC 6492 trade-supply-chain factoring operation classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, the relevant licensing and AML/CFT framework expects operational presence, compliance records, and personnel at a physical establishment. A virtual address may be used for auxiliary administrative correspondence only, not as the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% in the first 24 months of activity for a licensed trade-finance factoring company, with at least one unannounced compliance inspection expected per three-year supervisory cycle due to the enhanced AML/CFT risk classification and use of escrow and SWIFT payment rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 10, 11, 13, 20, 54, 99 and 103; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 5, 6 and 9.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts de constitution) and Initial Declaration (déclaration initiale) filed jointly through the Enterprise Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for cash, property or past services. The Business Corporations Act does not require an escrow account for incorporation, but any client funds received in the factoring business must be segregated in a dedicated escrow account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the corporation accepts the subscription for the incorporator and issues one hundred common shares as fully paid, for the assets contributed to the trade-supply-chain factoring business. RESOLVED that the registered office of the corporation be fixed at the address appearing in the Articles of Incorporation, and that the Secretary notify the Registraire des entreprises du Québec of any change. RESOLVED that the by-laws of the corporation be adopted as submitted, subject to shareholder approval. RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] be appointed Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Treasurer. RESOLVED that such officers are authorised to open bank and escrow accounts, execute factoring-related agreements, and file all statutory documents. Approved this day by the sole director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation corporate name search and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - online name search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a legal name reservation request through the online Enterprise Register portal. Review the proposed name against the Quebec enterprise name grid and include a declaration of non-confusion for the trade-supply-chain factoring business. The Registrar will issue a certificate of name reservation valid for 90 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, resubmit up to three alternative names with a distinguishability explanation; or request the name-review committee to reconsider the refusal within the prescribed delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles of Incorporation, initial by-law and registered office consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator or legal counsel; documents approved by the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles in either French or bilingual French/English in the form issued by the Registrar. Set the maximum number of shares and directors, restrict the factoring business if desired, and insert the registered office address in Quebec. Prepare the initial general by-law and the consent to act of the first directors and officers.
required_dossiers: Consent of the first director or directors
Registered office consent of the premises owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any drafting defect and resubmit to the Registrar; if the by-law conflicts with the Business Corporations Act, amend the by-law and obtain shareholder approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of Articles and Initial Declaration with the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - online Enterprise Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Enterprise Register, complete the articles filing form, attach the approved Articles and Initial Declaration, and pay the incorporation fee via electronic payment. Upon validation, receive the certificate of incorporation and the declaration number.
required_dossiers: Electronic access authorization for the filing representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is administratively queried or delayed, correct the missing fields using the online draft, respond to the Registrar's notice, and request re-registration; if the certificate is refused, appeal to the Court of Québec on a question of law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board resolution, share subscription and corporate minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office and corporate secretary; no government window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first board meeting or sign a written consent in lieu of meeting. Adopt the First Board Resolution for share issue, registered office and officer appointments. Issue share certificates in accordance with the subscribed share structure, and open a corporate minute book, share register and directors' register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum cannot be met, obtain a unanimous resolution of all directors; if a director resigns before completion, appoint a replacement under the Business Corporations Act and ratify the actions at the next shareholders' meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and social registrations with CRA and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec online business registration portals
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the certificate of incorporation to register for the federal Business Number, corporate income tax account, GST/HST account and, if hiring staff, payroll account. Register the same business with Revenu Québec for QST and provincial employer accounts, and complete the mandatory workplace health and safety registration.
required_dossiers: Bank account details for direct deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is not activated within the SLA, contact the business window or submit an account amendment; for most accounts the effective registration date can be backdated to the incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal commercial occupancy and fire safety clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal permits office and local fire-prevention service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a commercial occupancy permit application for the registered office, attach the lease, certificate of incorporation and site plan; arrange an on-site fire and electrical safety inspection, and obtain the occupancy permit and fire safety certificate before employees occupy the premises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If inspection results in non-compliance, correct the listed hazards, obtain a re-inspection, and request a temporary occupancy certificate while corrective work is completed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec for commercial registration; municipal permits office for premises; Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) only if ancillary lending or money-services activities are added
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Quebec Enterprise Registration Certificate (Attestation d'immatriculation) and municipal Commercial Occupancy Permit (Permis d'occupation commerciale)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC emissions or hazardous air pollutants are generated by factoring operations. Office waste must be sorted and disposed under municipal by-laws; electronic waste handled under MELCCFP regulation; HVAC emissions remain below annual reporting thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Commercial occupancy permit granted after municipal fire inspection; fire extinguishers, emergency exits, smoke detection and alarm inspection must be certified; building structural load certification supplied by the landlord; employer registration with CNESST for occupational health and safety and first-aid compliance.

mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as central bank, with monetary and exchange-rate policy administered under the Bank of Canada Act and the Currency Act; the Minister of Finance retains final authority on coinage and legal tender. Foreign exchange reporting and compliance are overseen by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, while cross-border currency and monetary instrument reporting is enforced by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free-floating exchange-rate regime with full convertibility on both current-account and capital-account transactions. The Currency Act and Bank of Canada Act impose no categories of restricted or blocked currency for trade and investment. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal: dividends paid to non-residents are subject to federal Part XIII withholding tax at 25% unless reduced by an applicable income tax treaty, and the payer must file an NR4 return and remit withholding within prescribed timelines. Interest, royalties, and management fees are also subject to Part XIII withholding, with treaty exemptions or reductions often available. Repatriation of capital from a Canadian business corporation is generally unrestricted, subject to corporate-law solvency tests, director approval, AML/KYC verification, and accurate valuation of the Canadian-dollar equivalent using the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement, mandatory conversion timeline, or minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds received by Canadian residents. Export proceeds and factoring settlements may be retained in foreign currency or converted at the corporate taxpayer's discretion. For income tax purposes, all proceeds must be reported in Canadian dollars using the Bank of Canada exchange rate or a rate acceptable to the Canada Revenue Agency. FINTRAC reporting obligations apply to cross-border electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, including factoring advances and export collections, and to any physical cross-border movement of currency or monetary instruments of CAD 10,000 or more.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada / Banque Nationale du Canada
Royal Bank of Canada / Banque Royale du Canada
Bank of Montreal / Banque de Montréal

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low as a primary banking or escrow relationship; Medium as an auxiliary payment and collection channel. Offshore digital EMIs are not authorized banks under the Bank Act, cannot accept legal deposits in Canada, and are not eligible for CDIC deposit insurance. They cannot provide a conforming Capital Escrow Account for Canadian corporate compliance or tax purposes. They may operate only as money services businesses or payment service providers after FINTRAC registration and compliance with the Retail Payment Activities Act, provincial private-sector privacy laws, and consumer-protection requirements. For trade-supply-chain factoring, an offshore EMI may support small-value receivable collections but must not hold principal escrow balances or serve as the sole liquidity clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A face-to-face interview is not an absolute statutory mandate, but in practice most Schedule I Canadian banks require an in-branch KYC meeting for non-resident corporations with a medium-risk or enhanced-risk profile, particularly for ISIC 6492 factoring entities. Remote account opening is possible only where the bank's onboarding policy permits video-based identity verification and enhanced due diligence, with notarized and apostilled or certified corporate documents delivered by courier. For initial capital escrow sign-off and execution of deposit and indemnity agreements, physical presence of at least one authorized director or senior officer is strongly expected by tier-1 Canadian banks, especially when ultimate beneficial owners are non-resident or beyond Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity arising from multi-tier corporate shareholders, trusts, or private foundations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified federal/provincial corporate registry extracts, complete UBO register, trust deed or declaration of trust, sworn affidavit of corporate control, notarized passports of all UBOs, organizational chart with ownership percentages, source-of-wealth statement, professional background-check reports, and a written explanation of the corporate structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds or insufficient economic substance for a large inbound capital injection or factoring advance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for the last two fiscal years, bank reference letters, confirmed factoring and purchase ledger, assignment and factoring agreements, underlying client invoices and commercial contracts, tax clearance certificates, detailed cash-flow projection, and evidence of operational infrastructure in Quebec.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media flags on counterparties, underlying commercial debtors, beneficiary jurisdictions, or invoice payers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-chain audit trail, fully populated sanctions and PEP screening results, OFSI/UN/EU and Canadian sanctions checklist, KYC files for all commercial debtors, jurisdiction-specific risk assessment, external legal opinion on sanctions exposure, and remediated adverse-media documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Factoring activity characterized as unauthorized lending, collection-agency activity, or unlicensed money services business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion confirming that the transaction constitutes a true sale/assignment of receivables rather than a loan, standardized factoring policies, AML program and compliance manual, provincial debt-collection permit if required under Quebec's Act respecting the recovery of certain debts, confirmation of any necessary FINTRAC MSB registration, and complete client onboarding and credit-underwriting records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital injections from non-resident shareholders are executed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers to a Canadian Schedule I bank account, using remittance information that clearly identifies the transfer as a 'capital contribution / share subscription under the Canada Business Corporations Act' and references the shareholder name, subscription agreement, and corporate file number. Canada imposes no exchange-control approval for equity injections, but FINTRAC reporting applies to electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; supporting verification includes the board resolution authorizing share issuance, subscription agreement, payment instruction, and bank confirmation. For inbound loans from non-resident related parties, a written shareholder loan agreement with arm's-length interest terms must be maintained; interest payments are subject to Part XIII withholding unless exempt under the Canada-US or other applicable treaty, and Form T106 must be filed for reportable transactions with non-resident related persons. The Bank of Canada daily exchange rate must be documented for Canadian-dollar recording of the injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for factoring settlements, supplier payments, and reverse-factoring advances are cleared through SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers for cross-border payments and through Lynx (High Value Payment System) for Canadian-dollar large-value payments. Documentary trade transactions use commercial letters of credit issued or confirmed by Canadian Schedule I banks, transmitted by SWIFT MT700, and governed by UCP600. Factoring disbursements must be supported by assignment schedules, invoice copies, client payment mandates, and a clear purpose code; all electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC, and records must include counterparty identifiers, source-of-funds documentation, and the economic purpose of the transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (CAD/USD and other freely tradable major currency pairs)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with restricted deliverability or for hedging emerging-market receivables
Cross-currency swaps, including cross-currency interest rate swaps
FX options (calls, puts, zero-premium collars, and structured vanilla combinations)
Flexible forwards with embedded optionality and early termination features

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to $100 CAD; potential corporate dissolution after two consecutive years of non-filing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required for public companies, reporting issuers, or corporations exceeding revenue/employee thresholds (typically gross revenue > $1 million or >50 full-time employees)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations; IFRS for public or large entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual maintenance and confirmation of share register and ultimate beneficial ownership information; required upon share transfers or regulatory requests under FINTRAC AML guidelines

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Quebec general corporate income tax rate of 26.5% (federal general rate 15% plus Quebec provincial general rate 11.5%). A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) earning active business income up to CAD 500,000 may qualify for the federal Small Business Deduction (federal rate reduced to 9%) and the Quebec small business reduction (Quebec rate reduced to 3.2%), producing a combined effective rate of 12.2%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income; federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable investment tax credit at 26% for qualifying CCPCs; Quebec innovation and e-business tax credits where eligible; no industry-specific tax holiday exists for trade finance or factoring activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal, CRA). Mandatory electronic filing through CRA-certified EFILE software; non-resident corporations file with the CRA's International and Large Business Directorate. The T2 is an annual federal return covering Part I corporate income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; taxation year is the corporation's fiscal period, which cannot exceed 53 weeks.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline: 6 months after fiscal year-end (s. 150(1) Income Tax Act). Balance-due day: generally 2 months after fiscal year-end for CCPCs and 3 months for other corporations; quarterly installments are required where the balance due exceeds CAD 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income (loss) from factoring operations as adjusted by the reconciliation of accounting income to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income attributable to a Canadian or Quebec permanent establishment; the Quebec factoring book, contracts, credit decisions, and employees must be identified to support PE income attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after application of non-capital loss carryovers, thin capitalization limits, and other deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments of factoring discount or interest to a non-resident related party must respect s. 18(4) thin capitalization (1.5:1 debt-to-equity) and be priced at arm's length; otherwise the deduction is denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I tax after federal abatement, Small Business Deduction, and investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are ineligible for the Small Business Deduction and must compute Part I tax only on the income allocated to a Canadian permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month overdue up to 12 months; repeat failure within 3 years: 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months. Gross negligence penalty (s. 163(2)): 50% of the understated tax. Failure to file an information return (e.g., T106 or NR4): CAD 100 per day up to CAD 25,000. Prescribed interest accrues on all unpaid amounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return (Revenu Quebec). E-filed through Revenu Quebec's certified software or the mandatory electronic transmission portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned with the federal taxation year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline: within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; payment due 2 months after year-end (CCPC) or 3 months after year-end; quarterly installments where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income, including allocation of business income to a permanent establishment located in Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on factoring business through a Quebec PE must file CO-17 and allocate income using the PE apportionment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec corporate income tax at 11.5% general rate or 3.2% reduced rate for small and medium-sized businesses, after the Quebec abatement and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced rate is unavailable to non-resident-owned corporations; compute tax at the general 11.5% rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on capital of financial institutions; an entity engaged in the business of acquiring receivables or financing trade debts may be classified as a financial institution under the Quebec Taxation Act and be subject to this tax on paid-up capital employed in Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute capital tax only on capital attributable to Quebec activities; a non-resident factoring corporation with a Quebec PE is within the charge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month overdue up to 12 months; repeat failure: 10% plus 2% per month up to 24 months. Gross negligence under the Quebec Taxation Act: 50% penalty. Interest is compounded daily.
